answer:
The preferred first-line urate-lowering therapy for recurrent gout, according to the ACR Guideline for Management of Gout (Management of Gout, ACOR, 2020) [ACR Guideline for Management of Gout, 2020], is allopurinol. This recommendation is made for patients with recurrent gout flares, tophi, or radiographic damage, and titrated to a serum urate target below 6 mg/dL.

Based on this guideline, allopurinol should be used as the recommended first-line agent in treating recurrent gout. Please note that this recommendation must be reviewed by a professional for clinical context and patient-specific suitability.
